raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation With the DiT offloaded to CPU, Cosmos3 can return a different image or video than with the DiT resident, for the same request and seed. `Cosmos3OmniTransformer.post_load_weights` builds the RoPE inv_freq table on the DiT's device, and only when the table is on meta; otherwise it keeps the one the constructor built on CPU. With `--dit-cpu-offload` or `--dit-layerwise-offload` the DiT is still on CPU at that point, so the table is computed on CPU. CPU and CUDA `pow` function round 5 of Edge's 64 entries one ulp apart (also similar for Nano and Super). The resident path and original NVIDIA's cosmos code (https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-framework) compute it on CUDA. Nobody noticed this problem because the offloaded output still looks fine, just a different render of the same scene, and the difference only happens at larger token positions. The Cosmos 3 GPU tests also run resident only. I found this while optimizing Cosmos 3 on DGX Spark (SGLang enables CPU offloading by default when serving Cosmos 3). Since Spark has unified memory, so I ran the experiments below on a 4090, which has separate VRAM and system RAM like most machines. ## Modifications Always compute `inv_freq` on `get_local_torch_device()`, then move it to the DiT's device. It stays float32 and non-persistent. On the normal meta-to-GPU load the values are the same as before. ## Accuracy Tests Settings: - RTX 4090 - Cosmos 3 Edge, BF16 - Two long prompts, each one paragraph repeated three times: T2I 640 * 640 and T2V 832 * 480 * 121, 35 steps | | T2I | T2V | |-|-|-| | main branch offloaded vs. main branch resident | PSNR 29.37 dB, SSIM 0.972 | PSNR 25.19 dB, SSIM 0.885 | | this PR offloaded vs. main branch resident | byte-identical | byte-identical | | this PR resident vs. main branch resident | byte-identical | byte-identical | ``` export SGLANG_DISABLE_COSMOS3_GUARDRAILS=1 sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge --dit-cpu-offload true # resident: --performance-mode manual ``` T2I prompt: ``` An overhead view of a busy harbor at golden hour. Dozens of small fishing boats in faded blue, red and white paint are moored along weathered wooden piers, their nets piled in loose heaps and their hulls reflecting in the calm green water. Gulls circle above a row of stacked wooden crates filled with silver fish, while workers in yellow rubber overalls carry baskets between the boats and a small market of canvas stalls. Long shadows stretch across the cobblestone quay, which is lined with narrow three-story houses painted ochre, teal and coral, each with flower boxes under the windows and laundry hanging on lines between them. In the distance a stone lighthouse stands at the end of a breakwater, and low hills covered with olive trees rise behind the town under a sky streaked with thin orange and pink clouds. The scene is sharp and detailed, with realistic textures on the wood, rope, stone and water, natural warm lighting, and a calm, lived-in atmosphere. ``` T2V prompt: ``` A first-person view from a small delivery robot rolling slowly along a sidewalk in a quiet residential neighborhood on a bright autumn morning. Maple trees with red and orange leaves line the street, and fallen leaves drift across the pavement in a light breeze. Parked cars, a blue mailbox, low garden fences and front porches with pumpkins pass by on the right side as the robot moves forward at a steady pace. A cyclist passes on the road to the left, and a person walking a golden retriever appears ahead and steps aside. The camera motion is smooth and stable, the lighting is natural with soft shadows, and the scene stays realistic and coherent from frame to frame. ``` main branch T2I result (resident vs. CPU offloading, and pixel difference by 4x), main branch T2V result (resident vs. CPU offloading, and pixel difference by 4x) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b76c2d5d-6e13-496f-a923-23b8a8d9c959 ## Speed Tests and Profiling Settings: - RTX 4090 - Cosmos 3 Edge presets from `bench_diffusion_denoise.py` - main branch code vs this PR in ABBA order. Seconds per warmed request (`total_duration_ms / 1000`), mean of two runs | Preset | resident | + `--dit-cpu-offload true` | + `--dit-layerwise-offload true` | |-|-|-|-| | Cosmos 3 edge t2i | 0.814 -> 0.821 | 1.370 -> 1.371 | 7.653 -> 7.635 | | Cosmos 3 edge t2v | 21.078 -> 21.109 | 21.764 -> 21.766 | 21.213 -> 21.230 | | Cosmos 3 edge i2v | 21.150 -> 21.133 | 21.766 -> 21.802 | 21.182 -> 21.217 | All within 1% ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41607709141](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41607709141) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41607709211](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41607709211) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :white_check_mark: [Run #41607709149](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41607709149) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. @AgainstEntropy I believe everything is all set, could you run CI? Thanks!
@AgainstEntropy The remaining CI failures is on Flux-3 disaggregated vs. monolithic on MI300. It fails the same way on other recent PRs. So it seems unrelated to this PR

@rwang5203 mentioned to me that the previous code adds 58 ms to the Edge DiT load with `--dit-cpu-offload`. With offload, `post_load_weights` was the first caller of the CUDA `pow` and reciprocal kernels, so it paid their lazy module load (~14 ms and ~4-7 ms). main never loads them. Building the table on CPU avoids that but changes the output again.

The new commit (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47442/changes/b3775d740bfeca64f2690898df40b08da09a0b55) use `torch.logspace` on CUDA when `head_dim` is a power of two (128 for all Cosmos 3 models). CUDA `logspace` calls the same `pow`, and with a power-of-two `head_dim` the exponents are exact in FP32, so the table is bit exact. `logspace` shares its kernel module with `arange`, which the forward loads anyway. The reciprocal runs on the DiT's device, and CPU and CUDA round it the same. Other cases keep the original code.

`post_load_weights` on a 4090, Cosmos 3 Edge:

| | main | previous (without the new commit) | now |
|-|-|-|-|
| resident | 32.8 ms | 32.7 ms | 9.4 ms |
| `--dit-cpu-offload` | 5.0 ms | 30.7 ms | 6.7 ms |
| `--dit-layerwise-offload` | 2.6 ms | 29.6 ms | 4.4 ms |

Over 20 paired fresh starts per mode, DiT load matches main (offload -0.5 ms, 95% CI [-8.5, +7.7]; layerwise median +1.4 ms). The ~1 ms left is the `arange` module load that main does in its warmup request, just moved earlier. Outputs are bit exact to main branch in all three modes, and request latency is unchanged.

@AgainstEntropy Could you check it out? Thanks so much!

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Shall we also update the docstring of `post_load_weights` above?

 from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.fsdp import is_module_list_entry_in
 from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.cache.conditioning import cached_conditioning

+    get_local_torch_device,
     get_sp_group,
     get_sp_world_size,

@@ -2004,31 +2005,43 @@ def _try_emit(linear_target: str):
             yield from _try_emit(linear_target)
 
     def post_load_weights(self, target_dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16) -> None:
-        """Cast non-quantized parameters to their preferred dtypes and rebuild
-        meta-device buffers.
+        """Cast non-quantized parameters to their preferred dtypes,
+        and rebuild the RoPE buffer.
 
         Time-embedder stays in float32 for numerical stability; embeddings and
         the VAE/LLM bridge linears go to ``target_dtype``. Quantized modules
         (e.g. FP8 from a ModelOpt export) are skipped — calling ``.to(dtype)``
         on them would cast their FP8 weights back to BF16/FP32 and break the
         quant kernels.
 
-        Also re-materializes the RoPE ``inv_freq`` buffer, which can land on
-        the meta device when the model is constructed under a meta context.
+        Also rebuilds the RoPE ``inv_freq`` buffer from powers computed on
+        ``get_local_torch_device()``, and places it on the DiT's device.
         """
         # Get the actual device from a loaded parameter
         device = next(self.parameters()).device
 
-        # Recompute RoPE inv_freq buffer on the correct device
-        # This is needed because model is created in meta device context
+        # Compute RoPE on the runtime device so offload preserves resident values
         rotary_emb = self.language_model.rotary_emb
-        if rotary_emb.inv_freq.is_meta:
-            dim = rotary_emb.head_dim
-            inv_freq = 1.0 / (
-                self.rope_theta
-                ** (torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) / dim)
+        dim = rotary_emb.head_dim
+        runtime_device = get_local_torch_device()
+        if current_platform.is_cuda() and dim & (dim - 1) == 0:
+            # CUDA logspace matches pow for power-of-two dims without its cold load.
+            # CPU and CUDA reciprocals round identically for these FP32 powers.
+            powers = torch.logspace(
+                start=0,
+                end=(dim - 2) / dim,
+                steps=dim // 2,
+                base=self.rope_theta,
+                dtype=torch.float32,
+                device=runtime_device,
             )
-            rotary_emb.register_buffer("inv_freq", inv_freq, persistent=False)
+            inv_freq = powers.to(device).reciprocal()
+        else:
+            exponents = torch.arange(
+                start=0, end=dim, step=2, dtype=torch.float32, device=runtime_device
+            )
+            inv_freq = (1.0 / (self.rope_theta ** (exponents / dim))).to(device)
+        rotary_emb.register_buffer("inv_freq", inv_freq, persistent=False)
 
         # Collect all quantized submodules so we can skip them during
         # dtype casts.  Calling .to(dtype) on a quantized layer would

     )
 
 
+class _RopeOnlyTransformer(torch.nn.Module):
+    _maybe_install_step_mixed_precision = (
+        Cosmos3OmniTransformer._maybe_install_step_mixed_precision
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, device, meta_rope, rope_theta, head_dim):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.rope_theta = rope_theta
+        self.hf_config = {}
+        self.modelopt_fp8_checkpoint = False
+        self.language_model = torch.nn.Module()
+        with torch.device("meta" if meta_rope else "cpu"):
+            self.language_model.rotary_emb = Qwen3VLTextRotaryEmbedding(
+                head_dim=head_dim, rope_theta=rope_theta
+            )
+        self.language_model.embed_tokens = torch.nn.Embedding(
+            num_embeddings=2, embedding_dim=2, device=device
+        )
+        self.time_embedder = torch.nn.Linear(
+            in_features=2, out_features=2, device=device
+        )
+        self.proj_in = torch.nn.Linear(in_features=2, out_features=2, device=device)
+        self.proj_out = torch.nn.Linear(in_features=2, out_features=2, device=device)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires CUDA/ROCm for CPU/GPU RoPE parity"
+)
+class TestCosmos3RopePlacement(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_rope_table_does_not_depend_on_dit_placement(self):
+        """A CPU-offloaded DiT must build the RoPE table a resident one builds."""
+        rope_theta, head_dim = 100_000_000, 128
+        exponents = torch.arange(
+            start=0,
+            end=head_dim,
+            step=2,
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device=get_local_torch_device(),
+        )
+        reference = (1.0 / (rope_theta ** (exponents / head_dim))).cpu()
+        for device in ("cpu", "cuda"):
+            for meta_rope in (True, False):
+                with self.subTest(device=device, meta_rope=meta_rope):
+                    model = _RopeOnlyTransformer(
+                        device=device,
+                        meta_rope=meta_rope,
+                        rope_theta=rope_theta,
+                        head_dim=head_dim,
+                    )
+                    Cosmos3OmniTransformer.post_load_weights(model)
+                    rotary_emb = model.language_model.rotary_emb

@AgainstEntropy The remaining CI failures is on Flux-3 disaggregated vs. monolithic on MI300. It fails the same way on other recent PRs. So it seems unrelated to this PR

@rwang5203 mentioned to me that the previous code adds 58 ms to the Edge DiT load with `--dit-cpu-offload`. With offload, `post_load_weights` was the first caller of the CUDA `pow` and reciprocal kernels, so it paid their lazy module load (~14 ms and ~4-7 ms). main never loads them. Building the table on CPU avoids that but changes the output again.

The new commit (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47442/changes/b3775d740bfeca64f2690898df40b08da09a0b55) use `torch.logspace` on CUDA when `head_dim` is a power of two (128 for all Cosmos 3 models). CUDA `logspace` calls the same `pow`, and with a power-of-two `head_dim` the exponents are exact in FP32, so the table is bit exact. `logspace` shares its kernel module with `arange`, which the forward loads anyway. The reciprocal runs on the DiT's device, and CPU and CUDA round it the same. Other cases keep the original code.

`post_load_weights` on a 4090, Cosmos 3 Edge:

| | main | previous (without the new commit) | now |
|-|-|-|-|
| resident | 32.8 ms | 32.7 ms | 9.4 ms |
| `--dit-cpu-offload` | 5.0 ms | 30.7 ms | 6.7 ms |
| `--dit-layerwise-offload` | 2.6 ms | 29.6 ms | 4.4 ms |

Over 20 paired fresh starts per mode, DiT load matches main (offload -0.5 ms, 95% CI [-8.5, +7.7]; layerwise median +1.4 ms). The ~1 ms left is the `arange` module load that main does in its warmup request, just moved earlier. Outputs are bit exact to main branch in all three modes, and request latency is unchanged.

@AgainstEntropy Could you check it out? Thanks so much!
